subject: Tokenflow evaluation & exit checklist
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: tokenflow evaluation and commit timeline

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a first-pass MAP focused specifically on the throughput evaluation we discussed (tokens/sec, sustained QPS, TTFT and concurrency). High level ask: confirm your sample traffic and what success looks like so we can lock a provably repeatable benchmark and a close milestone.

Proposed scope (short):
- Baseline run on your sample traffic (1M tokens) to measure tokens/sec and TTFT at 95th/99th percentiles.
- Sustained QPS run: 30-minute steady state at target concurrency (you suggested 120 concurrent users).
- Variant runs: 1) quantized model, 2) small-batch optimizations, 3) CPU fallback.
- Unit economics: per-M-token cost and cost at 1k/5k sustained QPS.

Owner & deadlines (draft):
- FinWave: provide 48h of representative JSONL traffic + any redaction rules (due: 2027-04-01).
- Redwood (Ben): run baseline + variants and produce results (due: 2027-04-04).
- Redwood (Marissa): summarize unit economics and recommend routing + caching knobs (due: 2027-04-05).
- Mutual sign-off and PO/DocuSign for Dedicated pilot (target: 2027-04-09).

Attachments: proposed_map_tokenflow.xlsx (MAP + milestones).

Questions for you:
1) Does the proposed 30-minute sustained run align with FinWave compliance for sample data?
2) Any hard constraints on peak concurrency or burst windows we should include?

If that looks good I can queue the baseline runs first thing tomorrow.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: tokenflow evaluation and commit timeline — bench plan + costing

Team / Oliver —

Attached is the bench plan and a preliminary unit-econ sheet (sustained_qps_costing_v2.xlsx, bench_plan.md). Key test harness details:
- Hardware: n4-standard (4xA100-equivalent) in us-west-2 for parity with Redwood Dedicated pool.
- Models: open-llama-70b (fp16), open-llama-70b-int8 (quantized).
- Batching: dynamic continuous batching with target batch windows tuned so median latency < 120ms.
- KV cache warm-up: 10k prefix tokens prior to sustained run.

Performance targets (working):
- Baseline tokens/sec: 38k–45k tokens/sec aggregated across the pool for the fp16 run at 120 concurrent sessions.
- Sustained QPS: 120 QPS (steady) — expect sustained token throughput of ~4.3M tokens/hour for 512-token avg context.
- TTFT target: median < 250ms, p95 < 600ms; tail (p99) action item if > 1.2s.

Unit economics (summary):
- Baseline (fp16): ~$0.95 per 1M tokens for dedicated pool if sustained QPS <= 250.
- Quantized (int8): reduces per-M-token to ~$0.58 but expect slightly higher p95 latency under high concurrency unless batching is tuned.
- Fallback to cpu/gpu mix for spikes: add ~15–25% margin on monthly committed spend.

Deliverables and timing:
- Baseline run + results CSV (throughput_results.csv) by EOD 2027-04-04.
- Consolidated MAP summary PDF by 2027-04-05.
- Draft PO/DocuSign for pilot by 2027-04-06.

I'll kick off the baseline tonight against the sample traffic Oliver sent.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@finwave.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Apr 2027 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: tokenflow evaluation and commit timeline — initial results

Oliver / team —

Quick update from the baseline runs. See throughput_results.csv attached and short summary below. Quoted below the bits from Ben's plan for context.

Summary (baseline fp16 run, avg 512-token requests):
- Aggregated tokens/sec: 41,600 tokens/sec (steady window 25–30 mins).
- Sustained QPS (measured): 125 QPS average; spike headroom observed up to 600 QPS for short bursts when batching engages.
- TTFT: median 220ms, p95 540ms, p99 1.18s (just below our 1.2s action threshold).
- Concurrency behavior: under steady 120 concurrency the runtime maintained KV cache hit ratio ~92% which helped tokens/sec.

Observations / action items:
1) Tail latency: p99 is close to threshold. We recommend enabling small-batch flattening + slightly larger batch windows for the quantized run to avoid tail regressions.
2) Cost: initial econ calc shows fp16 run maps to ~$0.97 / 1M tokens (aligns with Ben's sheet). Quantized int8 path projects down to ~$0.60 / 1M tokens but will need an extra pass on batching to hold p95 SLA.
3) Next step: run the quantized variant overnight and run a 30-minute sustained QPS test at 120 and at 600 QPS (burst profile) to validate headroom behavior.

Attached: throughput_results.csv (sampled windows + percentile latencies).

If FinWave is comfortable with the numbers, we can finalize the MAP and I will produce the one-page exit checklist for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
